answer: Each mining seat needs a bond locked in escrow for as long as its identity earns rewards, so a Sybil farm pays real capital per key: splitting one wallet into a thousand identities costs the same as a thousand honest miners, and any slashing burns that capital. Grading uses commit-reveal words (a cipher), so one script cannot be safely reused under many keys. An attacker must also produce unique correct work per seat, so sharing one stash of text like shale chips, or cloning one marble-hard template, is the fingerprint that triggers slashing.
